newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds remain weaker as Treasuries tumble.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds remain weaker as Treasuries tumble.

text.p: Irish government bonds weakened in thin trade on Friday as gilts and Bunds slipped after a tumble in the U.S. Treasury market, dealers said.
U.S. bonds dropped after the Chicago purchasing managers index showed a jump to 60.0 in August from 51.2 in July.
"We have underperformed gilts a bit but are steady against bunds. There has been a sell off in the 10-year area to the UK but that has not affected the spreads much," one dealer said.
"Europe seems to be holding up relatively well despite the tumble in the States. Things are pretty calm," the dealer added.
Dealers said U.S. traders were squaring their positions ahead of a holiday weekend.
"That has not helped the situation much," one dealer said.
By 1500 GMT the 8.00 percent bond due 2000 was seven pence lower at 103.58 to yield 6.86 percent. The 8.00 percent bond due 2006 was down 15 pence at 102.47 to yield 7.49 percent.
Dealers said the market was looking ahead to the release of key Irish credit data figures on Thursday.
